claim: TanStack Table is headless — no markup, no styles — so the design system stays authoritative; MUI DataGrid theming is only comfortable inside Material conventions.
quote: TanStack Table is headless by design: it owns no markup and no styles, so you own the entire visual layer and your design system stays authoritative... pushing it far outside Material conventions can become a fight against the component.

claim: shadcn/ui's data-table is TanStack Table wired into copy-paste components you own in-repo.
quote: shadcn/ui provides powerful table and datagrids built using TanStack Table... how to use TanStack Table and the Table component to build your own custom data table.

claim: AG Grid exposes --ag-* CSS custom properties that can reference your own tokens via var(); class-level custom CSS is fragile because DOM structure changes each release, and position/overflow/pointer-events are load-bearing.
quote: DOM structure changes with each release... custom rules you write may break. ... position, overflow and pointer-events control how the grid operates, and changing these will change how the grid operates, and may break functionality.

claim: Mantine React Table styles via mantine*Props, the emotion-backed sx prop, and inherits the Mantine theme's primaryColor/gray/dark scales.
quote: The sx prop is the recommended styling method... offers additional power through emotion styling. ... The table primarily leverages: primaryColor, gray shades, dark shades (for dark mode), and white for backgrounds.

claim: AG Grid's Theming API exposes 100+ theme parameters backed by CSS custom properties, with validation and TypeScript autocompletion.
quote: Themes created by the Theming API support over a hundred Theme Parameters. Under the hood, theme parameters utilize CSS custom properties (variables)... using the API provides benefits like validation and TypeScript autocompletion.

claim: Tailwind v4 puts utilities in a cascade layer, so unlayered/runtime-injected third-party CSS wins over utilities regardless of specificity.
quote: unlayered CSS beats layered CSS regardless of specificity

claim: MUI + Tailwind v4 requires enableCssLayer and an explicit layer order with mui before utilities.
quote: @layer theme, base, mui, components, utilities; ... the mui layer should come before the utilities layer.

claim: MUI's @layer support exists because MUI component selectors out-specify Tailwind utilities, previously forcing !important.
quote: Material UI v6 components have higher CSS specificity than Tailwind utilities, requiring developers to use !important flags... Material UI lacks a mechanism to properly override these layered styles.
